title: OMB federal AI policy memos M-25-21 and M-25-22 — summary record
notes: Summary record ingested from the official White House release (page dated April 7, 2025) and the OMB memoranda index, both fetched live 2026-11-09. Memo full texts are PDFs on whitehouse.gov and were not fetchable as text this session; M-25-21 PDF URL confirmed by fetch attempt (HTTP 200, application/pdf). publicationDate 2025-04-03 is the OMB memo date per the memoranda index; the release page is dated April 7, 2025. Executive-branch guidance, ingested as federal AI policy context — not legislation.

sections.heading: White House release summary (April 7, 2025)
sections.body: From the official White House release "White House Releases New Policies on Federal Agency AI Use and Procurement" (dated April 7, 2025 on the page), fetched live 2026-11-09: the White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB) released two revised policies on Federal Agency Use of AI and Federal Procurement, delivering on President Trump's decisive Executive Order to remove barriers to American leadership in Artificial Intelligence (AI); the memos were revised at the direction of the Executive Order and in coordination with the Assistant to the President on Science and Technology and the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP). The release frames the guidance as removing "unnecessary bureaucratic restrictions," allowing agencies to be "more efficient and cost-effective," and supporting "a competitive American AI marketplace" (Lynne Parker, Principal Deputy Director, White House OSTP), and cites a "widening gap in adopting AI and modernizing government technology" that the policies address (Greg Barbaccia, Office of the Federal Chief Information Officer). The release links: OMB Memorandum M-25-21, Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust; OMB Memorandum M-25-22, Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government; and a Fact Sheet, "Eliminating Barriers for Federal Artificial Intelligence Use and Procurement."

sections.heading: The memoranda (OMB memoranda index, checked 2026-11-09)
sections.body:
From the OMB memoranda index (https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/information-resources/guidance/memoranda/), fetched live 2026-11-09:
- M-25-21 Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust (April 03, 2025), with companion "Fact Sheet: Eliminating Barriers for Federal Artificial Intelligence Use and Procurement" (April 03, 2025).
- M-25-22 Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government (April 03, 2025).
Later AI-related memoranda on the same index: M-26-04 Increasing Public Trust in Artificial Intelligence Through Unbiased AI Principles (December 11, 2025); M-26-10 Reinforcing Transparency, Accountability, and Oversight of Federal Technology (March 31, 2026).
M-25-21 and M-25-22 are the operative executive-branch federal AI use and procurement policy baseline as of the fetch-check date; the index lists no later memo superseding them as of 2026-11-09.

sections.heading: Full text availability
sections.body: Both memoranda are published as PDFs on whitehouse.gov. M-25-21 PDF: https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/M-25-21-Accelerating-Federal-Use-of-AI-through-Innovation-Governance-and-Public-Trust.pdf (URL confirmed this session — a fetch attempt returned HTTP 200 with content type application/pdf; PDF text extraction is unsupported by this tooling). M-25-22 PDF is linked from the OMB memoranda index. Because the memo full texts could not be extracted as text, this record is a summary composed from the official release page and the OMB memoranda index — not the memo texts themselves.

sections.heading: Relevance to S. 5471
sections.body: M-25-21 and M-25-22 set the executive-branch baseline for federal AI use and procurement as of 2026-11-09; S. 5471 (introduced) would instead impose FTC-administered transparency mandates on commercial AI systems — a separate, legislative track. Context link: NIST's AI RMF page states AI RMF 1.0 "is being revised as part of the White House AI Action Plan" (checked 2026-11-09), so the NIST framework landscape this bill leans on is itself in revision. Collection note: executive-branch guidance ingested here as federal AI policy context; it is not legislation and not a bill.
